title: SWD Umpires
subtitle: Becoming a certified umpire is a valuable way to deepen your knowledge of the sport, support fair play, and strengthen competition across the Southwest Division. Umpires play an important role in maintaining standards on the green and helping clubs and tournaments run smoothly.

sections.heading: Why Become an Umpire?
body: Umpiring is not only about officiating matches. It is also about building confidence, improving your understanding of the game, and supporting your club and the wider bowls community.

items.title: Develop Expertise
items.body: Gain a stronger understanding of the Laws of the Sport, practical officiating procedures, and on-green decision making.

items.title: Support Fair Play
items.body: Help ensure competitions are played and officiated consistently, professionally, and fairly.

items.title: Give Back to the Game
items.body: Umpires provide an essential service to clubs, divisions, and tournaments, and help strengthen the sport at every level.

sections.heading: Rules, Laws & Learning
body: Start with Bowls USA guidance and domestic regulations, then use World Bowls resources to deepen your knowledge of laws, measuring, and umpire development.

sections.heading: How to Become an Umpire
body: The pathway begins with learning the role, reviewing the relevant laws and regulations, and then moving into training, assessment, and practical experience.

items: Learn the Role — Review Bowls USA umpiring information, domestic regulations, and the Laws of the Sport to understand the role and responsibilities of an umpire.
Build Your Knowledge — Study the official resources on laws, measuring equipment, procedures, and scorekeeping.
Complete Training & Assessment — Follow the applicable accreditation and assessment process for becoming a certified umpire.
Keep Developing — Continue learning through practical experience, refresher resources, UmpStumpers, and articles such as The Lawman.

body: Send an email request for more information and next steps.

migrationNotes: PRIVACY: the page publishes one personal Gmail address, mavizenor@gmail.com (Melanie Vizenor, SWD Head Division Umpire / National Umpire in Chief), as the contact for umpire enquiries. It appears three times on the source page (two buttons and a plain 'Or email' line). Worth a privacy review before republishing; a role-based address would be safer. No other personal contact details are published.

The umpire list itself is a published Google Sheet embedded as an iframe, kept as an embed section so it stays live. Its content is Name + Home Club only (24 umpires), with footnotes '*National Umpire in Chief' and '** SWD Head Division Umpire' against Melanie Vizenor. It could be converted to a static table section if we prefer not to depend on Google.

Two in-page anchor buttons on the source page ('View Resources' -> #swd-umpire-resources, 'Jump to Scorecard Guide' -> #swd-scorecard-guide) were dropped: the schema has no anchor-link concept and the target content follows immediately in the rendered page.

The email links on the source page point at a Gmail compose URL (mail.google.com/mail/?view=cm...), which forces Gmail on the visitor. Rewritten as ordinary mailto: links preserving the same recipient and subject lines.

The 'UmpStumpers' card links to the same Bowls USA laws page as the 'Bowls USA Laws & Umpiring' card, not to a dedicated UmpStumpers page. That is what the source does; may be worth a more specific link.
The 'Scorekeeping Guide' card on the source page was an anchor to the scorecard image below it, so it carries no link here.
The scorecard image is a 2021 Squarespace upload (SCORECARD Final.png); it should be checked that it still matches current scorecards.
